les: Al daardie water, en so min om te drink

items.bewering: Nie alle water op die aarde is dieselfde nie. Ons kry twee soorte water: soutwater en varswater.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Saline Water and Salinity' (usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/saline-water-and-salinity): for USGS purposes water under 1 000 mg/L dissolved solids is fresh and everything above it is saline, which is a two-way split. Tested as a set: brackish water (a mix, 0.5-35 g/L, e.g. SA's roughly 290 estuaries; marineprotectedareas.org.za/estuaries) sits between the lesson's 'baie sout' and 'baie min sout'. The lesson never says every body of water is one or the other, and it says 'die meeste' about lakes and wetlands, so nothing it states is false. This is a gap, not an error. No change needed.

items.bewering: Soutwater bevat baie sout en ons vind dit in die oseane.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's water?' (usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/where-earths-water): ocean water is saline. Walvis Bay Salt Refiners data (imformed.com Salt Forum 2023): seawater holds about 3.5% salts. Open University OpenLearn, 'Understanding water quality': seawater averages about 34 400 mg/L dissolved solids, against 118 mg/L for river water.

items.bewering: Mense kan nie soutwater drink nie
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Service, 'Can humans drink seawater?' (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/drinksw.html): drinking seawater can be deadly, because kidneys can only make urine less salty than seawater. AMNH OLogy, 'Why can't we drink seawater?': it makes you thirstier. 'Kan nie' is meant as 'cannot safely', which is the usual sense.

items.bewering: en die meeste diere en plante op land ook nie.
items.bron: Plants: halophytes (salt-tolerant plants) are about 2% of plant species at most, and under 0.2% can live with repeated seawater exposure. Most plants, crops among them, cannot survive a sixth of seawater's salt (Flowers & Colmer review, PMC4332615; Glenn et al. 1999, UC Davis). Animals: NOAA (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/drinksw.html) names only marine mammals and seabirds, which have special kidneys or salt glands, as able to drink seawater. 'Die meeste' is the correct quantifier.

items.bewering: Varswater is die water wat ons elke dag drink en waarmee ons kos maak en was.
items.bron: UNESCO, 'Water for Life' (webarchive.unesco.org): freshwater is the resource used for all social and economic activity. NOAA (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/drinksw.html): humans cannot drink seawater, so drinking water is fresh water.

items.bewering: Boere lei ook hulle gewasse met varswater nat.
items.bron: Minister Didiza's statement at the National Water and Sanitation Summit (dws.gov.za, 2022) and BusinessTech/DWS figures: agriculture uses more than 60% of South Africa's fresh water, nearly all of it for irrigation. The halophyte sources above show most crops cannot take salt water.

items.bewering: Varswater bevat baie min sout. Daar is wel 'n bietjie sout in, maar te min om sout te proe.
items.bron: USGS 'Saline Water and Salinity': fresh water is under 1 000 mg/L dissolved solids, so it does contain some. OpenLearn: average river water is 118 mg/L, and lakes and streams are typically 50-250 mg/L. WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality (TDS background): water under about 600 mg/L is palatable, and chloride's taste threshold is 200-300 mg/L (Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, NHMRC). So ordinary fresh water is well below the point where salt can be tasted. Water near the top of the fresh range can taste slightly salty. The sentence describes fresh water in general and is true of it.

items.bewering: Ons vind varswater in riviere en strome, in die meeste mere en die meeste vleilande, en ook in ys en onder die grond.
items.bron: Each item checked. Ice and groundwater: USGS 'Where is Earth's water?' says ice caps and glaciers hold about 68.7% of fresh water, and fresh groundwater is the next largest store. Glacial ice is fresh, and sea ice is much less salty than seawater. Rivers and streams: OpenLearn gives average river water at 118 mg/L. Lakes: Wurtsbaugh et al. 2017 (Nature Geoscience, 'Decline of the world's saline lakes') find saline lakes are 23% of lake area, so 'die meeste mere' holds (they are 44% of volume, mostly because of the Caspian). Wetlands: US EPA Report on the Environment / USFWS Status and Trends say about 95% of US wetlands are freshwater, and the Ramsar Global Wetland Outlook puts inland wetlands at about 77% of wetland area against about 10% coastal or marine. 'Die meeste' is correctly hedged for both lakes and wetlands.

items.bewering: Die meeste van die aarde se water lê in die oseane en daardie water is sout.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Where is Earth's water?' (usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/where-earths-water): oceans hold about 96.5% of Earth's water, and it is saline.

items.bewering: Van al die water op aarde is net 'n klein deel varswater wat mense kan gebruik.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's water?': about 2.5% of Earth's water is fresh, and most of that is locked in ice and underground. EarthDate, 'How Earth makes fresh water' (earthdate.org): 97.5% is salt water and 2.5% is fresh. The sentence is true whichever way it is parsed: 'only a small part is fresh water' or 'only a small part is fresh water that people can use'.

items.bewering: Varswater is dus baie skaarser as soutwater.
items.bron: USGS 'Where is Earth's water?': about 2.5% fresh against about 97.5% saline, so salt water is roughly 39 times more plentiful. The 'dus' follows from the sentence before it.

items.bewering: 'n Natuurlike hulpbron is iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik om in hulle behoeftes te voorsien.
items.bron: Collins English Dictionary via Dictionary.com, 'natural resources': 'naturally occurring materials such as coal, fertile land, etc, that can be used by man'. Freie Universitaet Berlin geolearning glossary, 'Natural resources': materials created in nature, usable by humans, including soil and water, that satisfy human needs and wants. The lesson's wording matches both.

items.bewering: Die hout van bome is 'n natuurlike hulpbron, en so is die grond waarin boere kos kweek.
items.bron: Dictionary.com/Collins: natural resources are 'the natural wealth of a country, consisting of land, forests, mineral deposits, water, etc.', with fertile land given as an example. FU Berlin glossary names soil explicitly. FAO (Director-General Qu Dongyu): at least 95% of global food production depends on soil.

items.bewering: Water is een van die belangrikste natuurlike hulpbronne wat ons het.
items.bron: UNESCO, 'Water for Life' (webarchive.unesco.org): 'Freshwater is the most important resource for mankind... a condition for all life on our planet'. National Water Act 36 of 1998, preamble (saflii.org): water is 'a scarce and unevenly distributed national resource' and a natural resource that belongs to all people. Some sources say 'most important' outright, so the softened 'een van die belangrikste' is safe.

items.bewering: Elke mens, dier en plant het water nodig om te lewe.
items.bron: NASA Astrobiology, 'What does life need for survival?' (science.nasa.gov/astrobiology/learning-resources/alp/what-does-life-need-for-survival/): 'All of the living things that we know of need food and water in order to stay alive'. The universal claim is safe because it says 'nodig', not 'drink'. Animals that never drink still need water and get it from their food or metabolism.

items.bewering: Jy het al gesien hoe nat wasgoed aan die draad in die son droog word. Die water in die klere verdwyn nie sommer nie. Die son maak die water warm en van die water verander in waterdamp.
items.bron: USGS, 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle' (usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/evaporation-and-water-cycle): 'Evaporation occurs when energy (heat) forces the bonds that hold water molecules together to break.' EarthDate: 'Heat and wind turn seawater into water vapor.' Checked as an analogy: washing drying in the sun maps soundly onto evaporation from rivers and the sea. Water is not destroyed, it changes into vapour, and the sun supplies the energy. The text never says water ONLY evaporates when the sun heats it, so a learner who sees washing dry in the shade has not been told anything false.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp styg op in die lug, maar jy kan dit nie sien nie.
items.bron: Invisible: water in its gas phase is transparent. Visible clouds and kettle 'steam' are liquid droplets (Wikipedia 'Water vapor'; Loughborough University, 'Cloud is a gas?', lbas.lboro.ac.uk). Rising: University of Wisconsin SSEC 'Weather Guys' (wxguys.ssec.wisc.edu, 2021-07-12): water vapour (18 g/mol) is lighter than dry air (29 g/mol), so moist air is less dense. EarthDate: 'The pure water vapor rises into the atmosphere'.

items.bewering: Ons noem dit verdamping. Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en die see.
items.bron: USGS 'Evaporation and the Water Cycle': evaporation is water changing from liquid to gas, and about 90% of the moisture in the atmosphere comes from evaporation from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers. Evaporation from soil is part of evapotranspiration on the same site.

items.bewering: Die son maak ook die seewater warm en van daardie water verdamp. Die sout kan nie saam met die waterdamp opstyg nie en bly agter in die see.
items.bron: EarthDate, 'How Earth makes fresh water': 'In the phase change from liquid to gas, water leaves salt and all impurities behind.' NASA Aquarius salinity education material (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov; earthdata.nasa.gov 'Salt of the sea'): when seawater evaporates, the salt is left behind and salinity rises. Wind-blown sea spray does carry salt particles into the air, but that is spray, not vapour, and the sentence is about the vapour.

items.bewering: Jy kan dit self sien as jy 'n bakkie soutwater in die son laat staan. Na 'n ruk is die water weg en lê daar 'n wit lagie sout in die bakkie.
items.bron: This is how solar salt is made. Walvis Bay Salt Refiners (imformed.com Salt Forum 2023; projectblue.com) evaporate seawater in sun-heated pans and get 99.4% pure sodium chloride. NASA Aquarius: when salt water evaporates the salt is left behind. Checked as an analogy, the bowl standing for the sea, and the mapping holds. The bowl dries out completely, while the lesson says only some ('van daardie water') of the sea evaporates, so the text does not suggest the sea dries up.

items.bewering: Daarom bevat die waterdamp uit die see geen sout nie.
items.bron: EarthDate: 'The pure water vapor rises into the atmosphere'. Salts do not evaporate, which is the same NASA/EarthDate basis as above, so the absolute 'geen' is correct for the vapour. Tested as a chain with the next two sentences: rain does pick up a trace of dissolved matter (OpenLearn gives about 7 mg/L for average rainwater), but the lesson never says rain or fresh water is salt-free. It says fresh water holds 'n bietjie sout', so the chain is consistent and adds up to nothing false.

items.bewering: Die waterdamp vorm later wolke wat reën gee.
items.bron: EarthDate: the vapour 'condenses into clouds as it encounters cooler conditions. It then falls back to Earth as fresh water.' NASA Earth Science water cycle (gpm.nasa.gov/education): ocean water evaporates, travels as clouds or vapour over land, and falls as rain or snow.

items.bewering: So kom baie van ons varswater eintlik uit die sout see.
items.bron: Link et al. 2020, Earth System Science Data 12, 3177 (essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3177/2020): on average 51% of land precipitation evaporated from land, so roughly half comes from ocean evaporation. EarthDate: Earth's fresh water exists because the water cycle desalinates seawater. 'Baie van' (much of), not 'al' (all), is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: soutwater: Water met baie sout in, soos die water in die oseane.
items.bron: Read on its own: true. NOAA and USGS (above) say ocean water is saline at about 35 g/L. 'Soos' gives an example, not a full list. The entry agrees with the study text.

items.bewering: varswater: Water wat baie min sout bevat, soos die water in riviere en die meeste mere.
items.bron: Read on its own: true. USGS defines fresh water as under 1 000 mg/L dissolved solids, which is little but not none, matching 'baie min'. River water averages 118 mg/L (OpenLearn). Saline lakes are a minority by area (Wurtsbaugh et al. 2017), so 'die meeste mere' is correctly hedged. The entry agrees with the study block.

items.bewering: natuurlike hulpbron: Iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik om in hulle behoeftes te voorsien.
items.bron: Read on its own: true, on the same basis as the study-block definition (Dictionary.com/Collins; FU Berlin geolearning glossary). The wording is identical to the study text.

opsomming: All 26 claims are confirmed against sources. Tested as a set, the salt-water and fresh-water contrast holds: evaporation leaves the salt behind, the vapour is pure, rain feeds the fresh water, and fresh water still has 'a little salt', so the chain never says fresh water or rain is salt-free; every 'die meeste' is the right quantifier. One gap for a person to know about, not an error: brackish water (estuaries) falls between the lesson's two definitions, and the lesson never claims otherwise.
